$comment: Accepted survivors for scripts/mutation-check.mjs: mutants on changed lines that no test kills because the change is equivalent (behaves the same) or harmless. An entry matches on file, mutator, original and replacement text (whitespace collapsed), not on line number. Each entry needs a reason. The check prints a ready-made entry for every new survivor; add one only after deciding a test cannot or should not catch it. See docs/quality.md.

Equivalent: moment.tz reads an empty zone name as UTC, so the default zone and "" give the same dates.

Equivalent in the safe.* refusal: configKey is null only when the option is neither `-c` nor `--config-env`, and then `/^safe\./i.test(null)` tests the text "null", which never starts with `safe.`, so the refusal is the same either way.

Equivalent: for an `env -S` string that does not start with an option, checking `env` followed by its words reads the same command as checking the words alone, because checkSegment looks through env to the program it runs; an empty string gives `env` plus the rest of the line, which is the rest of the line. Every allowed and blocked `env -S` row decides the same either way.

Equivalent: the text before `=` is a shell variable name, which can hold a `+` only as its last character (the `NAME+=` append form; bash rejects any other `+` as an invalid identifier), so removing the first `+` and removing a trailing one give the same name.

Equivalent for a variable name: `.*` is greedy, so without `$` it still removes everything from the first `[` to the end of the word. The two differ only for a word holding a line break, which bash does not accept in a name.

Equivalent for this repository: the guard reads `env -S`/`--split-string` itself (guard-bash.mjs, the env split-string branch) before the reader's wrapper walk sees it, so every allowed and blocked env -S row decides the same either way. This file is a pinned copy of the canonical reader (shell-reader.test.mjs checks its sha256, and is left out of the mutation run for that reason), so a real change to its reading lands and is tested in the canonical copy.
